name: near
description: NEAR Protocol as one mod. NEAR's personality is its account model: accounts are human-readable names (alice.near) or 64-hex implicit accounts, an account and a contract are the same object, and access keys carry per-contract permissions — session auth on chain. This module reads all of it (balances with staked and storage-locked NEAR priced in USD, access keys, contract methods parsed from the deployed WASM export section, view calls, NEP-141 tokens, history, transactions, validators) and now writes all of it: a keystore under ~/.mod/near/, contract deploys with a batched init call (redeploying upgrades in place), signed change calls with gas and deposit, transfers, account creation (testnet faucet mints funded *.testnet names; elsewhere sub-accounts of the signer), access-key management. Writes default to testnet; a non-testnet write refuses without confirm=true; a write over HTTP needs the token from ~/.mod/near/token. ed25519 via PyNaCl with a pure-Python RFC 8032 fallback, borsh in-tree — still zero hard dependencies. Eighteen MCP tools, a REST API and a browser console run the same code on one port.

endpoints.call_change: POST /call {contract, method, args?, gas_tgas?, deposit_near?, token}

backend: python stdlib only (http.server + urllib); WASM export-section parser, borsh serializer and RFC 8032 ed25519 in-tree (PyNaCl used when present)
auth: reads open; writes sign with keys from ~/.mod/near/ (never the repo) — non-testnet writes refuse without confirm=true, HTTP writes need the token from ~/.mod/near/token, secret keys never leave the keystore

env.PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 50910)
env.NEAR_RPC: your own RPC endpoint — skips the public failover pool
env.NEAR_OFFLINE: skip the tests that need the chain
